photos.credit: Vezzerina (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Large harvested adult hung tail-up over a boat rail at a tuna ranch, seen from the back/side. Row of yellow finlets with dark edges along the tail stalk, very short sickle pectoral fins, dark blue-black back, silver flank with chainmail-like pattern, blood near gills and head cut.
photos.species_basis: Short pectorals, yellow finlets + caption: harvested Atlantic bluefin tuna, tuna ranch in Turkey
photos.use: Anatomy of finlets and pectoral length from above. Hanging dead fish with blood: do not copy pose, wounds or boat rail into natural scenes.

photos.credit: Kürschner (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Whole dead adult lying left side up on ice in a glass display case, head left. Thick fusiform body, dark blue-black back, silver sides, short pectoral fin ending well before the second dorsal fin, low second dorsal, small yellowish finlets toward tail. Dark low-key light, glass reflection line across the body, gill area slightly opened/reddened, small spoon with food at left edge.
photos.species_basis: Short pectoral and thick body consistent with Thunnus thynnus + caption: Atlantic bluefin aquaculture research project display
photos.use: Identity of body shape and pectoral length. Dead fish on ice: do not copy display case, ice, glass glare or dull post-mortem colour into living scenes.

photos.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Native Fish of Indiana; FWS digital media library)
photos.observed: Studio photo of an adult on a pure white background, full right side, all fins spread. Very deep compressed body, concave nape, large oblique mouth; dense irregular black speckles and blotches over silvery-green sides, no regular bars; dorsal, anal and caudal fins with light-dark checker pattern; spiny dorsal low, about 7 spines visible. Even soft light, sharp.
photos.species_basis: Irregular speckles instead of bars, deep body, ~7 dorsal spines; USFWS label.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for pattern, fin shape and body depth. White cut-out background and flash-even lighting are not scene elements; underwater colour will be darker and less contrasted.

photos.credit: André Giraldi (iNaturalist photo 205692806, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult in a clear observation box of water, outdoors, left side. Erect spiny dorsal with 7 countable spines connected to the soft dorsal; olive-gold back, black blotches and speckles on head and sides, yellow-and-black checkered dorsal, anal and caudal fins; anal fin nearly as long as dorsal. Box edges and reflections visible.
photos.species_basis: 7 dorsal spines counted, irregular blotches; iNaturalist research-grade observation 121546590 (3 IDs, California, 2022-06-12).
photos.use: Best reference for dorsal spine count and live fin colours. Box walls, glass reflections and grass background must not appear in scenes.

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Juvenile, 59 mm SL per caption (North Fork Muddy Creek, Maryland, 2014-04-14), left side on a plain grey background. Yellowish-silver body, fine dark speckles scattered irregularly on the sides, no vertical bars; spiny dorsal with about 6-7 visible spines joined to a large soft dorsal; checkered soft dorsal, anal and caudal fins. Specimen appears freshly preserved or anaesthetised (fins slightly ragged).
photos.species_basis: Irregular speckling and spine count consistent with black crappie; SERC specimen label with standard length.
photos.use: Juvenile proportion and pattern. Size from caption (59 mm SL) is not a profile size row; lab background and pale tone are not scene elements.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Underwater three-quarter close-up of head in hatchery tank: smooth blue-grey skin without spots, large silver eye, nasal and long maxillary barbels, white lower lip, upper jaw longer than lower. Rear body and anal fin out of frame; background soft green blur.
photos.species_basis: USFWS label; unspotted blue-grey head and jaw consistent with blue catfish. Anal fin not visible, so anatomy role only.
photos.use: Anatomy of eye, barbels, mouth and skin tone in water. Do not use alone to separate from channel catfish.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Whole adult, left side, cut out on black background (Gavins Point NFH). Blue-grey back fading to pale belly, no scattered spot pattern (two isolated tiny dark specks only, not a channel-type spotting), long anal fin with straight outer margin, deeply forked tail, straight-sloping predorsal profile to wedge head, upper jaw overhangs. Even light, no occlusion.
photos.species_basis: Visual: unspotted body + long straight-edged anal fin + wedge head; USFWS label.
photos.use: Identity reference for anal fin shape, head profile and colour. Black studio background: do not copy into natural scenes; do not add the isolated specks as spots.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Hatchery fry on black background, side view: translucent grey body with fine melanophore speckling (not channel-type round spots), iridescent gut area, forked tail, long-based anal fin, short barbels. Sharp, no occlusion.
photos.species_basis: USFWS hatchery label (Gavins Point NFH); forked tail and long anal base consistent. Fry-stage separation from channel fry is not verifiable by eye here.
photos.use: Fry-stage proportions and translucency. Not a scale reference; do not render adult-type spots on blue juveniles. Role limited to production: fry cannot be told from channel catfish fry visually (label-only ID).

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult, full left side on black studio background, fins spread. Solid black ear flap with no red/orange edge, small upturned mouth ending before the eye, deep compressed disc-shaped body, long pointed pectoral, joined spiny and soft dorsal, faint vertical bars, olive-brown body with orange-yellow breast. Soft-dorsal blotch not clearly visible in this light.
photos.species_basis: Visual: black ear flap without red margin, small mouth, body shape, no wavy cheek lines; labelled bluegill by USFWS hatchery photographer.
photos.use: Primary identity and anatomy reference (ear flap, mouth, fin layout). Do not copy black studio background or flash lighting into natural scenes; breast colour here is not proof of sex.

photos.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service ('Native Fish of Indiana', via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: In-water photo over gravel and leaf litter in greenish water; one adult in three-quarter side view centre frame, two more bluegill blurred in background. Black ear flap, blue-grey lower jaw and cheek, bright orange-yellow breast, faint scale spotting, small mouth. Fish fills about a third of the frame.
photos.species_basis: Visual: black ear flap, small mouth, deep body, blue lower jaw; USFWS label.
photos.use: Reference for natural underwater colour, turbidity and small loose group. Orange breast suggests a breeding-coloured fish; do not make every bluegill orange-breasted.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Two hatchery fingerlings lying in a wet open palm, heads up-right, hatchery raceway blurred behind. Deep compressed bodies, small mouths, clear dark vertical bars over greenish-silver flanks, pale throats. Each fish roughly finger length; ear flap small and not distinct at this size. Commons original is 7008x4672 (>15 MB); this is the Commons 3840 px rendition.
photos.species_basis: Hatchery label 'Bluegill Fingerlings' plus visible deep body, small mouth and vertical bars; ear-flap mark not readable, so identity rests partly on label.
photos.use: Juvenile body shape, bar pattern and relative size against a hand. Do not copy the hand or hatchery setting into wild scenes; not a reference for adult colour. Role limited to production: hatchery fingerlings, marks too small; label-only ID.

photos.credit: Eric Engbretson, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Adult facing right over rounded cobble, dark background. Dense pale vermiculation on back and dorsal fin, pale yellow spots, a few small red spots, pectoral/pelvic/anal fins red-orange with white then dark leading edge, near-straight caudal. Slightly hooked lower jaw. Tail and fin of a second pale fish intrude at right edge.
photos.species_basis: visual marks (vermiculation, white-black fin edges, light spots on dark ground) + USFWS label
photos.use: Primary identity ref for pattern and fin edges. Do not copy the second fish at frame edge or the studio-dark backdrop into stream scenes.

photos.credit: James St. John (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Full-body side view facing right, captive coaster brook trout (Lake Superior Aquarium). Olive-gold flank with dense yellow spots and scattered red spots with blue halos, vermiculated back and dorsal, red lower fins with crisp white leading edge and black band, reddish caudal. Dark tank background, some particles in water.
photos.species_basis: visual marks + uploader label (captive coaster form)
photos.use: Shows brighter colouring and full fin edges; captive fish, so do not take tank lighting as natural stream light.

photos.credit: Karelj (own work, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Adult facing left in an exhibition aquarium (Prague 2011), blue tank wall. Clear head and mouth profile with open jaw showing teeth line, marbled orange dorsal fin, yellow spots and red spots with blue halos, white-edged pelvic and anal fins, adipose fin visible. Rocks at bottom, filter pipe top right.
photos.species_basis: visual marks + exhibit label
photos.use: Anatomy ref for head shape, mouth, dorsal marbling and adipose fin. Do not copy the blue tank or equipment.

photos.credit: John J. Mosesso (NBII Image Gallery, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Small young brook trout lying in an open palm with a dry fly in its mouth. Dark oval parr marks along the flank, small pale and a few reddish spots, pale lower fins; hand and sleeve fill most of the frame, no face visible.
photos.species_basis: NBII label Salvelinus fontinalis + light spots on dark ground; juvenile marks not covered by an opened A/B source
photos.use: Identity ref for juvenile pattern and scale against a hand. Do not reproduce the fly-in-mouth or the hand unless the scene is angling.

photos.credit: Knowledgemattersnow (own work, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Close-up of head and front half of a golden-yellow adult held out of water by a dark-gloved hand, blurred stream behind. Black and red-brown spots on gill cover and flank, some with pale halos; large mouth reaching behind the eye; yellow pectoral fin; water dripping. Tail and rear body out of frame.
photos.species_basis: visual marks (haloed dark spots, jaw past eye, no vermiculation) + uploader label
photos.use: Anatomy ref for head, jaw length, gill-cover spots. Out-of-water angler hold: use only for angling scenes; not a swimming or colour-under-water ref.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Whole fish facing left on black studio background (Garrison Dam NFH stock, US). Olive-gold body, dense dark brown/black spots on back and flanks with orange-red spots on lower flank, red-orange adipose fin, square caudal with few spots, no vermiculation, no white fin edges. Mouth slightly open, body gently curved.
photos.species_basis: visual marks (dark spots on light ground, red adipose, square tail) + USFWS label
photos.use: Primary identity ref for spot pattern and fins. Hatchery fish on black backdrop: do not copy backdrop or the bent pose as a swimming pose.

photos.credit: Gilles San Martin (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Underwater side view of head and front two-thirds of an adult facing left, dark green water. Grey-olive back, yellow cheek, large round black spots and scattered small red spots on flank, pectoral and pelvic fins pale; dorsal fin at top right; tail out of frame. Likely aquarium or clear stream, not stated.
photos.species_basis: visual marks (black and red spots on light ground, no vermiculation) + uploader label (stream form fario)
photos.use: Ref for underwater colour and spot density in natural-looking light. Tail not visible, so pair with SIDE-01 for fin shape.

photos.credit: Johann Jaritz (own work, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Several young fish in a glass bowl of water on a blue surface, Carinthia, Austria. Two front fish in side view show dark oval parr marks, yellowish lower body, small red spots and reddish adipose/fin tips; others blurred by glass refraction. Each fish is small in the frame.
photos.species_basis: uploader label Salmo trutta lacustris + visible red spots and yellow underside; parr marks not covered by an opened A/B source
photos.use: Juvenile pattern ref only; fish are tiny in frame and seen through glass. Do not copy the bowl, crowding or bright surface; European lake form, not a US stream fish. Role limited to production: small fish through glass, European lake form.

photos.credit: Brian Gratwicke (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Tight close-up of head through aquarium glass: open mouth, upper jaw overhanging lower, nasal and maxillary barbels, chin barbels, large eye, olive-grey head with white lips. Body, tail and anal fin out of frame. Slight glass haze.
photos.species_basis: Commons label (Rock Creek, DC); head shape and jaw consistent with channel catfish. Spots/anal fin not visible, so not an identity reference.
photos.use: Anatomy of mouth, barbel positions and eye. Do not use to decide species; do not copy aquarium haze.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Whole adult, left side, cut out on white background (hatchery fish, Gavins Point NFH). Dark slate-grey back, white belly, a few small discrete black spots on upper flank, deeply forked tail, short anal fin with rounded outer margin, long barbels, upper jaw overhangs lower. Even studio light, no occlusion.
photos.species_basis: Visual: scattered small black spots + rounded anal fin + forked tail separate it from blue and flathead; USFWS label.
photos.use: Identity reference for body shape, fins and sparse spotting of a mid-size adult. White cut-out background: do not copy studio look or flat pose into underwater scenes.

photos.credit: Kevin Stertz, Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Small juvenile (finger-length) lying on an open palm above water; silvery body with distinct round black spots along flank, deeply forked tail with dark edge, long barbel, dark back. Hand fills most of frame; fish occupies a diagonal band.
photos.species_basis: Visual: round black spots + forked tail (blue juveniles unspotted outside Rio Grande); ODFW label.
photos.use: Juvenile spotting and colour. Hand gives rough scale only, not a measurement; do not copy the hand-hold into natural scenes.

photos.credit: Laura Mahoney, USFWS Pacific Southwest Region (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Adult winter-run Chinook held by hands at a hatchery, head and front half toward camera, mouth wide open. Dark mouth interior and black gum line along the teeth of the lower jaw, hooked worn snout tip, olive-bronze head with black spots, dense spots on back, yellow tag on dorsal fin. Truck and hatchery tank in background; no faces.
photos.species_basis: Visual: black gums and back spotting; USFWS caption adult winter Chinook at Livingston Stone NFH.
photos.use: Head/mouth anatomy (black gums, teeth, kype). Do not copy the dorsal tag, hands or hatchery setting.

photos.credit: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa (collections.tepapa.govt.nz/object/840404)
photos.observed: Museum specimen, ocean-bright adult, full left side on plain grey background with 10 cm scale bar. Dark blue-green back, bright silver flanks, small black spots on back and dorsal fin, dark caudal fin (spots on lobes not resolvable), dark lining inside lower jaw, adipose fin present.
photos.species_basis: Te Papa collection label Oncorhynchus tshawytscha; visual: back spotting, dark gum line, body depth.
photos.use: Ocean/lake-phase identity and proportions; scale bar is the specimen's, not a default size. Dead specimen pose and flat light; do not copy into live scenes.

photos.credit: Roger Tabor, USFWS Pacific Region (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Underwater in a clear spring-fed stream: spawning adults over gravel and green weed. Main fish full side: olive-bronze body with dark vertical blotches and iridescent sheen, dense black spots on back, dorsal and both caudal lobes, black gum line with teeth on lower jaw, slightly hooked snout. Two more Chinook behind, one darker.
photos.species_basis: Visual: spots on both tail lobes and black gums (checked at full resolution); USFWS caption Chinook returning to McAllister Springs, WA.
photos.use: Spawning-phase identity, tail spotting and gum anatomy in natural light. 3840 px Commons thumbnail of a >15 MB original; do not copy weed layout as a fixed set.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Single juvenile on white background, left side, fins spread. Silvery body with faint grey parr marks crossing the lateral line, small dark spots on back and dorsal area, forked translucent tail, large eye.
photos.species_basis: USFWS caption juvenile Chinook at Gavins Point NFH; visual parr marks and salmonid shape (species not separable from coho by eye at this stage).
photos.use: Juvenile/smolt identity and proportions. Studio background only. Role limited to production: juvenile salmonid marks not decisive visually; label-only ID.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Close-up of head and front body on white, fish facing right. Large terminal mouth closed, maxilla running back under the eye to about/just past its rear margin; gold eye; dark blotches on upper side and dark streak behind the eye; smooth cheek with scales similar to body.
photos.species_basis: Visual: blotch pattern and gold eye; USFWS label at Gavins Point.
photos.use: Mouth, eye and cheek anatomy. Crop hides tail and dorsal; pair with the side photo for identity.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Studio shot on white, adult (caption: 5-6 lb, Gavins Point NFH aquarium) in left-facing three-quarter side view. Upper jaw clearly extends past the rear margin of the eye; broad midlateral row of dark blotches; olive mottled back, white belly; spiny and soft dorsal separated by a deep notch; gold-ringed eye. Mouth slightly open. No occlusion.
photos.species_basis: Visual: jaw past eye, blotched horizontal stripe, deeply notched dorsal (excludes smallmouth/spotted); USFWS label. Northern hatchery stock (South Dakota).
photos.use: Primary identity and jaw-length reference. White studio background and slightly open mouth are photo artefacts; do not copy into habitat scenes.

photos.credit: USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery) via Wikimedia Commons
photos.observed: Live adult swimming in an aquarium, true right-side profile on dark background. Dark midlateral band broken into blotches from gill to tail, plain silvery lower sides without rows of spots, deep dorsal notch, gold eye. Mouth closed; jaw end sits around the rear part of the eye in this pose. Light pinkish colour cast from lighting.
photos.species_basis: Visual: blotched horizontal band, deep dorsal notch, no lower-side spot rows; USFWS label.
photos.use: Underwater body-proportion and swimming-posture reference. Colour cast is aquarium lighting; natural water should read greener.

photos.credit: USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons
photos.observed: Two hatchery fingerlings of different size lying on a wet palm, right-side view. Blotched dark midlateral band, speckled green back, silvery belly; smaller fish shows bicoloured tail with darker outer part; larger fish jaw reaches past eye. Hand fills the background; fish not in water.
photos.species_basis: Visual: blotched horizontal band and bicoloured juvenile tail (not tricoloured as in smallmouth/spotted); USFWS caption "largemouth bass harvest".
photos.use: Juvenile colour and pattern reference. Out-of-water handling shot: do not copy hand, flattened fins or dry posture into natural scenes. Resized 1920 px Commons thumbnail of a 2470x1852 original.

photos.credit: Hans Hillewaert (Wikimedia Commons, own work)
photos.observed: Five dead landed fish packed in a blue crate, oblique top view. Top fish shows a tall, steep forehead (bull-type); another fish has a rounded sloping yellow head (cow-type). Colours faded to dull yellow-olive and grey with dark spots. Fish overlap each other; tails and heads partly cut by crate edges.
photos.species_basis: Long dorsal fins, forked tails, spotting, head shapes; uploader label Coryphaena hippurus from Dominica market
photos.use: Anatomy: male vs female head profile and post-mortem colour. Not a live-colour or swimming reference; individual sex not confirmed by dissection.

photos.credit: Hugues Evano, IFREMER Délégation océan Indien (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Whole fish in left-facing side view, isolated on a plain white background (appears cut out). Single dark dorsal fin from nape almost to tail, deeply forked tail, concave anal fin, slender tapering body. Back pale blue with many small dark blue spots, golden blotches along mid-flank and head; head profile rounded/sloping. Post-capture colours. File is small in bytes for its pixel size, consistent with a flat white background.
photos.species_basis: Single long dorsal fin, slender body (depth well under a quarter of length), concave anal fin, spotting pattern; Ifremer label Coryphaena hippurus
photos.use: Identity of fin layout and body outline. Do not copy the white cut-out background or the faded post-capture blue/white as live underwater colour.

photos.credit: Distad (Wikimedia Commons, own work)
photos.observed: Freshly caught adult held horizontally by an angler on a boat, left-facing full side view spanning most of the frame width. Rounded sloping forehead, green-gold flanks with fine dark spots and pale spots on lower flank, dark full-length dorsal fin, deeply forked tail. Angler's face visible behind the fish but not dominant; rods and reel at frame edges.
photos.species_basis: Single dorsal fin nape-to-tail, slender body, colour/spotting; rounded head matches the female description; file title says female
photos.use: Identity and female (cow) head shape. Do not copy the angler, boat or hands into natural scenes.

photos.credit: gendereuphorbia (iNaturalist photo 254881543, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live fish swimming right in an aquarium, near side view against blue water. Live colouring: yellow-green flanks, silvery-blue upper back, scattered small dark spots, dark-edged long dorsal and anal fins, forked tail. Sloping (not square) forehead. A strand of algae and red seaweed overlaps the upper mid-body slightly; blurred orange light at right.
photos.species_basis: Long single dorsal fin, slender body, live colour pattern; title and iNaturalist label Common Dolphinfish
photos.use: Live colour reference under water. Aquarium setting and seaweed are not habitat evidence; size not measurable.

photos.credit: James St. John (Wikimedia Commons, via Flickr); captive, Lake Superior Aquarium, Duluth, Minnesota
photos.observed: Aquarium shot through glass: head and front third of an adult, left side, head to the left, mouth closed. Long flattened duckbill snout, eye set mid-head, gill cover and pectoral fin (pointed tip) clearly visible, lateral line pores along flank. Body bronze-tan almost without pattern (clear phase). Lower jaw sensory pores and cheek scaling not resolvable; slight glass glare and warm cast.
photos.species_basis: Aquarium label Esox masquinongy (photographer caption). Visually consistent with muskie (duckbill snout, unpatterned clear phase, pointed fin); unpatterned fish cannot be separated from every hybrid by eye alone, so the label carries the ID.
photos.use: Head/snout shape and clear-phase colour reference. Do not use for jaw-pore counts or cheek scale coverage; do not copy the aquarium rock background or glass glare into wild scenes. Role limited to production: soft focus, clear phase, label-only ID; jaw pores/cheek scaling not visible.

photos.credit: Eric Engbretson / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult underwater in a sparse weed bed, full right side, head to the right. Dark irregular spots/blotches on a light silver-olive body (spotted phase), dense on rear half and caudal peduncle; pointed caudal lobes; dorsal and anal fins set far back near the tail; long duckbill snout; rusty-tinged pelvic/anal fins. Weed stems cross the tail and pelvic area; cheek scaling not resolvable. Original file replaces the earlier 1280 px thumbnail (same Commons file).
photos.species_basis: Visual: dark-on-light markings and pointed tail lobes exclude northern pike (light spots on dark) and tiger muskie (rounded fins, dark bars on light); USFWS label Esox masquinongy.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for the spotted phase in natural weed-bed habitat. Barred and clear phases are also valid; do not force spots on every muskie. Not a scale reference.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel / USFWS, Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery (USFWS Mountain Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Slender young fish on pure white background, full right side, unobstructed, sharp. Dark olive-brown blotches and faint bars on pale olive-silver body, forked caudal with pointed lobes and dark speckles on fin rays, dorsal and anal fins far back, long duckbill snout. Fish spans ~85% of frame width but is thin, so much of the frame is white. Length not stated.
photos.species_basis: Visual: dark-on-light blotches and pointed tail lobes; hatchery label Esox masquinongy. Stage judged juvenile from slender fingerling form; exact size unknown.
photos.use: Juvenile identity reference. White studio background is presentation only; take size from the profile table, not from this image.

photos.credit: Gilles San Martin (Wikimedia Commons, via Flickr)
photos.observed: Aquarium close-up of head and front body, left side, head to the left, mouth slightly open with small teeth visible at tip. Long flattened duckbill snout, paired nostrils, scaled cheek, gill cover with sensory pores, pectoral and pelvic fins; light bean spots on olive flank behind the head. Very sharp at full resolution; soft grey background.
photos.species_basis: Visual: bean-shaped light spots on darker olive body, scaled cheek; photographer label Esox lucius. European specimen of the same circumpolar species.
photos.use: Anatomy reference for snout, eye position, cheek/gill-cover scaling and head pores. Do not use pores visible here as a fixed count; aquarium background not for wild scenes.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel / USFWS, Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery (USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Studio shot on white, fish in water swimming diagonally up-right, full left side, head lower left, tail breaking a splash at top right. Rows of light bean-shaped spots on dark olive-green flanks, pale belly, orange-yellow fins with dark bars and rounded tips, moderately forked tail, duckbill snout, dorsal and anal fins far back. Fine scales visible over the cheek. Sharp; body diagonal so length reads foreshortened slightly. Size not stated.
photos.species_basis: Visual: light-on-dark bean spots and rounded fin tips exclude muskie and tiger muskie; no chain pattern (pickerel); USFWS caption Northern pike. Stage judged adult/subadult from proportions; length unknown.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for colour pattern and fins. White background and surface splash are studio presentation; do not copy into natural scenes. Not a scale reference.

photos.credit: Atelier Nespoulous (Wikimedia Commons, own work)
photos.observed: Young pike on pure black background, full right side, unobstructed, all fins spread. Small light spots in rows on olive-green flanks, pale belly, rounded fin tips, moderately forked tail, duckbill snout, dorsal and anal fins far back; a short dark mark below/behind the eye. Size not stated.
photos.species_basis: Visual: light-on-dark spots and rounded fins; title Jeune brochet (young pike). Stage juvenile from title and slender form; exact size unknown.
photos.use: Juvenile identity reference. Black background is studio presentation. The dark mark near the eye is visible on this fish but is not a sourced pike field mark; do not exaggerate it into a pickerel-style bar.

photos.credit: Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Several adult rainbow trout seen from above-side through clear shallow water over gravel. Main fish lower centre in full side view: olive back densely spotted, spots on dorsal and caudal fins, clear pink-red lateral band, red gill cover, slightly forked tail. Sunlit caustics and surface ripple.
photos.species_basis: Visual: dense black spots incl. tail, pink lateral band, no red haloed spots; ODFW label 'Rainbow Trout'.
photos.use: Resident/stocked rainbow identity and spot/band pattern. Group in clear pool; do not copy the surface glare or turn it into a steelhead (silver) scene.

photos.credit: Peter Oelschlaeger (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Fresh steelhead held horizontally by two hands over a river, left side. Bright silver body, faint pink-lavender lateral band, fine black spots on back and dorsal/adipose fins, pale lower jaw. Tail base held by hand; fishing line visible; sun glare top left. No faces.
photos.species_basis: Visual: silver body with faint pink band and back spots fits steelhead form of O. mykiss; labelled steelhead from Snake River.
photos.use: Steelhead identity (silvering, faint band, size impression ~24 in class). Do not copy hands, line or net into natural scenes.

photos.credit: Jennifer Strickland, USFWS Pacific Region (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Close-up of a steelhead head, right side, mouth open. Pale/white mouth lining and gums, maxilla extending past the eye, few dark spots on head, pinkish-red cheek, wet glossy skin; out of water at a hatchery.
photos.species_basis: Visual: light mouth and gums (not black like Chinook), jaw reaching behind eye; USFWS caption steelhead at Abernathy Fish Technology Center.
photos.use: Head/mouth anatomy: jaw length, pale gums, eye, cheek colour. Out-of-water hatchery shot; do not copy the hand or background.

photos.credit: Rob Holm, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Dense school of hatchery rainbow fry underwater, many in side view. Each shows a row of dark oval parr marks along the side, small dark spots, olive-gold body, large eyes. Dark background, artificial light.
photos.species_basis: Visual: oval parr marks and body shape of salmonid fry; USFWS caption Hot Creek rainbow trout at Garrison Dam NFH.
photos.use: Juvenile identity (parr marks, proportions). Hatchery density is not a natural stream scene. Role limited to production: juvenile salmonid marks not decisive visually; label-only ID.

photos.credit: Geeklikepi (Wikimedia Commons, own work)
photos.observed: Dead adult on wet sand, full left side, head right. Bronze-gold back fading to silver-white belly, low blunt snout, no chin barbels, two black spots: one at upper caudal base, one mid-body under the soft dorsal. Strong low sun and cast shadow; another fish and a cooler at frame edge.
photos.species_basis: Visual: caudal-base ocellus, no barbels, long low body; uploader caption says mature red drum from Louisiana Gulf coast.
photos.use: Identity and colour/spot-count variation (two spots valid). Do not copy beach setting, dead pose, harsh sun or the cooler into underwater scenes.

photos.credit: Warren E. Savary, U.S. Food and Drug Administration (Regulatory Fish Encyclopedia)
photos.observed: Fresh specimen, full left side on white studio background with Kodak colour card and 10 cm bar. Dark grey-bronze back, silver-green cheek, single small black spot at upper caudal base, orange-red pectoral, pelvic and anal fins. At full resolution the head is sharp: inferior horizontal mouth, blunt snout, scaled cheek, smooth preopercle edge, no barbels under the chin.
photos.species_basis: Visual: caudal ocellus, inferior mouth, no chin barbels; FDA RFE specimen label.
photos.use: Head/mouth anatomy (mouth position, no barbels) and single-spot identity. Studio colour card, scale bar and white background are not scene content; the 10 cm bar is not a sourced size of a typical fish.

photos.credit: Olivier Dugornay, IFREMER (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Split-level fisheye shot of a broodstock maturation tank: about 20 live adults swimming over a pale tank floor in green water; worker with a dip net above the waterline (face small, not dominant). Fish show coppery-silver bodies, caudal-base spot on several fish, one fish with a row of many small spots along the upper side. Water tint and fisheye distortion.
photos.species_basis: IFREMER caption (red drum broodstock, Antilles aquaculture) plus visible caudal spots, body shape, no barbels.
photos.use: Live swimming posture, group spacing and spot-count variation in water. Captive tank, green tint, net, person and fisheye are not wild habitat; do not use as Gulf/Atlantic scene reference. Role limited to production: aquaculture tank, fish small and green-cast.

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Flickr)
photos.observed: Juvenile (150 mm SL per caption) in clean lateral view, head left, fish fills the narrow frame edge to edge. Silver body with faint longitudinal scale-row lines, strong black spot at upper caudal base plus one small spot under the soft dorsal, fins spread, mouth slightly open and low, no barbels. Plain grey background.
photos.species_basis: Visual: caudal ocellus, no barbels, low mouth; SERC specimen label (Rhode River, MD, 2012).
photos.use: Juvenile identity and fin/mouth anatomy. Silver juvenile colour; do not apply adult copper tone. Plain background is presentation only. Original is 3484x1014 (short side under 1080), so 720p tier.

photos.credit: Totti (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Close-up of head and front body in a Japanese public aquarium, fish facing right. Bronze-gold colour, dark bars from eye across cheek, small cheek scales, jaw ending below the eye. A grey aquarium pipe stands in front of the snout on the right; small particles in water.
photos.species_basis: Visual: eye bars, jaw not past eye, small cheek scales; uploader label (introduced population exhibit, Aquamarine Inawashiro).
photos.use: Mouth-length and cheek-bar anatomy. Do not copy the pipe or aquarium particles. Resized 3840 px thumbnail of a 4032x3024 original.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS (USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Studio shot on white, left-side full profile. Dark bars radiating back from the eye across the cheek, olive-brown body with mottled vertical blotches, no continuous horizontal stripe; connected dorsal fins; upper jaw ends below the eye; eye dark brown in this lighting.
photos.species_basis: Visual: eye bars, vertical blotches, connected dorsal, short jaw; USFWS label.
photos.use: Pattern and fin-shape reference. White background and studio colour are artefacts. Eye is not red here: red eye is common, not mandatory.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS Mountain-Prairie via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult in an aquarium, right-side profile on dark background with rock. Uniform bronze-brown body, faint darker vertical shading, no horizontal stripe, no rows of spots; red eye; spiny and soft dorsal broadly connected with a shallow notch; jaw ends below the eye. Fins fully spread, no occlusion.
photos.species_basis: Visual: red eye, connected dorsal, jaw not past eye, no lateral stripe (excludes largemouth/spotted); USFWS label.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for bronze colour phase in clear water. Vertical bars can be faint as here; do not force strong bars.

photos.credit: JasperWV (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live juvenile in a planted native-fish aquarium over sand and pebbles, right-side view. Tricoloured tail (orange/yellow base, black bar, pale edge), mottled brown blotches, red-orange eye, dark bar from eye. Fish occupies about half the frame width; a plant stem crosses below the belly.
photos.species_basis: Visual: tricoloured juvenile tail and red eye (Iowa DNR mark for young smallmouth); uploader label.
photos.use: Juvenile identity reference. Aquarium decor is not a natural habitat reference. Resized 3840 px Commons thumbnail of a 5472x3648 original.

photos.credit: Rennair (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Freshly caught adult lying on a white boat deck, full left side. Dense round black spots on the upper half of the body, soft dorsal fin and caudal fin; dark caudal margin; silvery belly without spots; greenish-grey back; large oblique mouth with projecting lower jaw, yellowish mouth edge; yellow pectoral fin. Hard sunlight with cast shadow; landing net at left edge.
photos.species_basis: Visual: round spots on upper body extending onto dorsal and caudal fins, black tail margin (not weakfish/sand seatrout) + Commons label (adult caught in Gulf of Mexico).
photos.use: Identity reference for spot density, fin spots and mouth shape. Out-of-water dead pose: do not copy the deck, net, shadow or flattened fins into underwater scenes.

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Juvenile specimen (label: 92 mm SL, Honga River MD, 2012-07-11) on light grey background, left side filling the frame. Irregular dark blotches and spots along the upper flank, spotted dorsal and caudal fins, silvery belly, large golden eye, pointed snout with projecting lower jaw. Small water droplets on background.
photos.species_basis: Visual: spotted upper body and fins, projecting lower jaw + SERC specimen label.
photos.use: Juvenile identity: spots are larger and more blotchy than in adults. Specimen pose only; not a live-swimming reference.

photos.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (via public-domain-image.com, Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult in an aquarium, full left side over gravel with plastic plants. Seven to eight continuous dark stripes from gill to tail, several reaching the caudal base; slender body; dark olive back, silver sides, white belly; deeply notched dorsal; dark forked tail. Even light, slight film-scan softness.
photos.species_basis: Visual: continuous stripes reaching tail, slender body (not hybrid/white bass) + USFWS label on Commons.
photos.use: Main identity reference for stripe count, stripe continuity and body depth. Do not copy aquarium gravel or plastic plants into natural scenes.

photos.credit: PlanespotterA320 (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Swimming adult, left side slightly toward camera, dark tank background with rocks. Continuous dark stripes along silver flank, slender body, olive head, forked tail; mouth slightly open. Low light, mild noise, a second fish blurred behind.
photos.species_basis: Visual: continuous stripes, slender body + Commons label (National Aquarium, Baltimore).
photos.use: Reference for swimming posture and how stripes read in low underwater light. Do not copy the dark tank background or the blurred second fish.

photos.credit: Lee Weigt, Smithsonian NMNH / Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Fresh juvenile specimen (label: 90 mm SL, Rhode River MD, 2011-10-13) on grey background, left side, fills the frame. Silvery body with faint thin dark stripes on the upper flank, large eye, forked tail, two dorsal fins visible. Fins slightly folded.
photos.species_basis: Visual: slender silver body with faint longitudinal stripes + SERC/NMNH specimen label.
photos.use: Juvenile identity: stripes are faint at this size, body silvery. Do not give juveniles bold adult stripes; not a live-pose reference.

photos.credit: Zoltán Stekkelpak (iNaturalist photo 42717896, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Close-up of the head of a landed fish lying on a wooden board, right-facing. Long beak-like jaws slightly open showing a row of small, closely set triangular teeth; large eye; snout about as long as the rest of the head; pectoral fin base at left. Skin faded grey-silver with blotches (post-mortem).
photos.species_basis: Beak snout proportion and fine serrated tooth row; iNaturalist label Acanthocybium solandri
photos.use: Anatomy of jaws, teeth and snout length. Faded colour is post-mortem, not live colour.

photos.credit: Jeffrey Williams, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution (via U.S. FDA Flickr, Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Dead museum specimen USNM 445301 lying in a dark tray, full left-facing side view filling the frame. Long beak, raised long first dorsal with many spines, finlets, keeled peduncle, forked tail. Dark irregular bars still visible on dull silver flank; skin scuffed. Specimen tag and photographer credit printed in the image.
photos.species_basis: Museum catalogue label USNM 445301 Acanthocybium solandri plus beak, long first dorsal and bars
photos.use: Whole-body proportion and fin count reference. Dead specimen colour and printed labels are not for live scenes.

photos.credit: Michael Bommerer (Wikimedia Commons, own work)
photos.observed: Live adult swimming left in open blue water, clean side view, sharp. Long pointed beak-like snout, very slender body, about two dozen wavy dark-blue vertical bars on silvery-blue flanks, first dorsal folded low, small second dorsal and finlets toward tail, narrow peduncle, sharply forked tail. Small baitfish scattered in background; reef slope blurred below. Fish spans about 70% of frame width.
photos.species_basis: Beak-like snout, vertical cobalt bars, slender scombrid body with finlets; uploader label Acanthocybium solandri
photos.use: Primary live identity and swimming posture reference. Background baitfish/reef not habitat evidence for a given scene.

photos.credit: michael_bommerer (iNaturalist observation 250469347, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult swimming left in clear blue water near the surface, slightly angled side view. First dorsal fin raised, showing it is long and low with many spines; bars fainter than in UNDERWATER-01 due to light angle; beak snout, finlets and forked tail visible. Canary Islands.
photos.species_basis: Beak snout, long first dorsal, finlets, faint vertical bars; iNaturalist label Acanthocybium solandri
photos.use: Anatomy of the raised first dorsal fin; bar contrast varies with light, do not erase bars entirely in live fish.

photos.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Mountain-Prairie Region (Flickr)
photos.observed: Live adult head breaking the surface of a turbid brown river at water level, mouth open, head fills most of the frame. Large glassy eye with gold rim, nostrils, dark peppering on cheek and lower jaw, pink mouth lining, a sharp canine visible near the front of the lower jaw. Sun glints on water; native camera resolution (Canon PowerShot D30, 4000x3000).
photos.species_basis: USFWS caption (walleye, Missouri River, 2014); head shape, eye and canines agree, but sauger shares these, so label-based.
photos.use: Head, eye and mouth/canine anatomy for reveal or strike scenes, and how the eye looks in daylight (no glow). Not an identity reference; surface pose and bank are not scene defaults.

photos.credit: Eric Engbretson, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
photos.observed: Live adult underwater over dark gravel, full right side, head right; second walleye partly behind. Olive-gold body with brassy vermiculated mottling, large glassy eye, long jaw, white tip on the lower caudal lobe clearly visible. Spiny dorsal folded, so the rear dorsal blotch is not visible; no spotted rows visible on the dorsal.
photos.species_basis: Visual: white lower tail tip and no dorsal spot rows exclude sauger; torpedo body without perch bars; USFWS label.
photos.use: Primary identity reference in natural underwater light. The dorsal blotch must come from the text checklist, not this image. Dark background and a vertical post at top are not habitat evidence.

photos.credit: Rob Holm, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Garrison Dam NFH)
photos.observed: Dense school of live fingerlings underwater in green water over vegetation, many fish in side and oblique views. Slender bodies with olive-brown mottling and faint dark saddles, large reflective eyes, translucent fins; individual fish occupy a modest part of the frame, some motion blur and suspended particles.
photos.species_basis: USFWS caption (walleye fingerlings reared at Garrison Dam NFH, 2019); slender percid body and large eyes agree.
photos.use: Juvenile colour, mottling, body proportion and schooling density. Hatchery rearing pond density is not a wild default; no size scale in the image. Role limited to production: species from hatchery label only; sauger fingerlings look similar.

photos.credit: Fizzishin (iNaturalist photo 443220333, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Freshly caught adult, full left side on a white measuring board (fish reaches about the 10.5 in mark). Silvery body with olive back and faint dark marks grouped into regular vertical bars; deep compressed body, concave nape, large oblique mouth, upper jaw past middle of eye; checkered caudal and soft dorsal. Spiny dorsal partly folded, spines not countable. Daylight, sharp.
photos.species_basis: Regular faint vertical bars on silver sides (not scattered speckles); iNaturalist research-grade observation 248095191 (3 IDs, Trenton MI, 2024-10-19); Commons label.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for pattern and body shape. Out of water on a board: do not copy the board, the dry pose or flattened fins into underwater scenes.

photos.credit: -Rorey- (iNaturalist photo 381674514, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Adult held in an open hand, right side, fins erect. Strongly contrasted dark vertical bars on a blue-green iridescent body, darker head; erect spiny dorsal shows about six spines; large rounded dorsal and anal fins set back, checkered fins. Person's sleeve and a tackle box in background; no face.
photos.species_basis: Vertical bars and ~6 dorsal spines visible; iNaturalist research-grade observation 215849714 (3 IDs, Iowa, 2024-05-14). Dark tone fits spawning-season darkening reported for males [S3, S4], but sex not confirmed.
photos.use: Shows bar pattern and fin spines at their clearest and a darker spring tone. Do not make this dark blue tone the default colour; hand and background are not scene elements. Role limited to production: dark spawning colour with dense blotches; on second review bars vs speckles not decisive, keep out of identity.

photos.credit: Fishes of Texas team (iNaturalist photo 453185302, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Small juvenile (a few cm) lying on a palm, left side. Slender silvery-iridescent body, large eye, dorsal and anal fins set far back opposite each other, forked tail with dark edge; no bars developed yet. Fish fills about half the frame width.
photos.species_basis: Genus-level marks (fins set back, large eye, oblique mouth); species rests on Fishes of Texas team identification, iNaturalist research-grade observation 253129220 (3 IDs, Colorado County TX, 2024-11-23). Visible marks alone cannot exclude black crappie at this size.
photos.use: Juvenile body proportion and colour only. Do not add adult bars or deep body to fish this small; do not use to separate the two crappie species. Role limited to production: juvenile marks cannot exclude black crappie; label-only ID.

photos.credit: Robert Colletta, USDA Agricultural Research Service (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult in an aquarium over pink gravel, three-quarter front view. Closed mouth without visible canines, large golden eye, olive head, strong regular dark bars on yellow flanks, spiny first dorsal with dark front membrane, orange pelvic and anal fins, lateral line visible.
photos.species_basis: Visual: bars, yellow colour, orange lower fins, spiny dorsal; USDA-ARS caption names Perca flavescens.
photos.use: Head, eye and mouth shape plus fin colour from the front. Mouth is closed, so it does not show teeth; do not copy aquarium gravel or glass reflections.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Live adult, full left side on black background, fins raised. Golden-yellow to olive flanks with about seven broad, regular dark vertical bars, white lower belly, two separate dorsal fins (spiny first dorsal with dark membrane), orange pelvic and anal fins, slightly forked tail with no white lower-lobe tip, no visible canines.
photos.species_basis: Visual: regular 6-8 bar pattern, yellow colour, separate dorsals, orange lower fins, no walleye tail tip; USFWS hatchery label.
photos.use: Primary identity reference for bar count/spacing, colour and fin layout. Do not copy black studio background or flash light into natural scenes.

photos.credit: Ken Hammond, USDA (via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Two perch over rounded pebbles against a dark tank background (Quantico, VA). Front fish angled head-down toward camera, raised spiny dorsal, dark bars on olive-gold flanks, orange pectoral/pelvic fins; second fish facing camera at right. Bars partly washed out by angle and lighting; likely aquarium, not wild.
photos.species_basis: USDA caption 'Yellow perch' plus visible bars, separate spiny dorsal, orange lower fins, no canines.
photos.use: Reference for in-water posture, fin carriage and a small group near the bottom. Bar count is not readable here; use SIDE-01 for marks. Do not copy the black backdrop.

photos.credit: USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Hatchery worker's palm holding a translucent gelatinous egg mass with many small eggs, strands dripping into a turbid pond; sunken evergreen branch at right, plastic bag behind. Accordion folding is not clearly readable.
photos.species_basis: Caption: USFWS hatchery yellow perch eggs about to hatch, placed on sunken evergreen trees; gelatinous strand matches S4/S5. Identity rests on the label.
photos.use: Texture and translucency of perch egg strands and the cover they are draped on. Do not copy the hand, bag or hatchery handling into wild spawning scenes. Role limited to production: egg mass ID from caption only.

photos.credit: Sam Stukel, USFWS Mountain-Prairie (Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery, via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Portrait frame: three hatchery fingerlings held side by side in a wet palm, heads up, hatchery raceway blurred behind. Slender olive-green bodies with faint, mottled dark vertical bars, little yellow, pale bellies, separate spiny dorsal partly visible, mouths slightly open without canines. Fish occupy the middle third of the frame. Commons original is 4672x7008 (>15 MB); this is the Commons rendition at that URL.
photos.species_basis: Hatchery label 'Yellow Perch Fingerlings' plus faint bar pattern and perch body form; low yellow fits S4 note that young perch are less yellow. Identity rests partly on label.
photos.use: Juvenile body form, muted colour and size against a hand. Do not give juveniles the bold yellow and sharp bars of adults; do not copy hand or hatchery setting. Role limited to production: hatchery fingerlings, bars faint; label-only ID.

photos.credit: Hugues Evano, IFREMER Délégation océan Indien (Wikimedia Commons / Archimer)
photos.observed: Whole adult, left side, head left, on a white cut-out background (background removed). Long sickle-shaped yellow second dorsal and anal fins, row of bright yellow finlets with dark edges above and below the tail stalk, iridescent golden-yellow lateral band, dark blue back, silver belly, long pectoral reaching past the second dorsal origin.
photos.species_basis: Long yellow sickle fins, yellow finlets, golden band, long pectoral + IFREMER caption Thunnus albacares (Réunion)
photos.use: Primary identity for large adult yellowfin. Background is digitally removed: do not copy white void; colours are of a freshly landed fish.

photos.credit: NOAA SEFSC Pascagoula Laboratory; Collection of Brandi Noble (NOAA Photo Library)
photos.observed: Fresh adult on wet dark deck plates, left side, head left, measuring board above. Yellow finlets with dark edges, yellow second dorsal and anal (moderate, not very long), long pectoral, faint golden band behind head, silver flank, dark blue back.
photos.species_basis: Yellow finlets, long pectoral, golden band + NOAA caption: Yellowfin tuna, Gulf of Mexico
photos.use: Identity of a moderate-size Gulf of Mexico yellowfin without elongated fins. Measuring board is not a sourced scale reference.

photos.credit: Marc Taquet, IFREMER (Wikimedia Commons / Archimer)
photos.observed: Dense school of live tuna swimming right-to-left in blue water near the surface, several fish large in foreground. Yellow finlets, yellow second dorsal and anal tips, long dark pectorals, silver flanks with blue backs; golden lateral band weak underwater. Fish are inside a purse seine off the Seychelles (net not prominent in this frame).
photos.species_basis: Yellow finlets and fins, long pectorals + IFREMER caption Thunnus albacares school, Seychelles
photos.use: Live underwater appearance and school density. Captured in a seine, so crowding is denser than free schools; other tuna species may be mixed in the background; Indian Ocean, not a US location ref. Role limited to production: purse-seine school may include other tunas; Indian Ocean, not a US setting.

photos.credit: Jeffrey Williams, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution (via U.S. FDA / Wikimedia Commons)
photos.observed: Juvenile specimen on grey studio background, left side, fins spread. Short (not sickle) second dorsal and anal fins, faint yellow tinge on second dorsal tip, row of finlets, moderately long dark pectoral, pale vertical bars/spots on lower flank, dark back. Colours faded/greyish post-mortem; label text LUZ-026 USNM-445243 in corner.
photos.species_basis: USNM catalogued specimen label Thunnus albacares juvenile + pale vertical lower-flank marks and finlet row
photos.use: Juvenile proportions and fin shape. Faded museum colours: do not copy grey tone or label text; pair with live adult refs for colour. Role limited to production: faded museum juvenile; yellowfin vs bigeye juveniles not separable by eye here, label-only ID.
